feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: U.S. employers add only 29,000 jobs in September, much less than August
entry.summary: The Labor Department offered an update Friday on the strength of the U.S. job market. The news comes as long-term interest rates have been climbing.

entry.title: Economist discusses high bond yields and the September jobs report
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks to Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics, about high bond yields and the September jobs report.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: September jobs report to give an update on the market, Tennessee governor halts executions after woman survives attempt, N.Y. attorney general appointed as special prosecutor in Cornell rape case.

entry.title: Dance Theatre of Harlem returns to Africa for first time in 3 decades
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Robert Garland, artistic director of the Dance Theatre of Harlem, a company where he was once principal dancer and that he is taking back to the African continent for the first time since the 1990s.

entry.title: Supreme Court to begin new term with cases on religion, guns and immigration ahead
entry.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court opens a new term, with test cases on religion, guns, immigration and climate change ahead.

entry.title: Google launches satellite to test feasibility of building data centers in space
entry.summary: Google has launched an experimental satellite that will test the feasibility of putting AI data centers in space.

entry.title: Car crimes in San Francisco have dropped. The city says Flock cameras have helped
entry.summary: Car crimes have plunged in San Francisco over the last four years. The city credits, in part, Flock cameras. We investigate the claim.

entry.title: Weakening of the Voter Rights Act has charged a surge in Black voters
entry.summary: Since the 2024 election, Black voters have led a surge in Democratic voter enthusiasm by responding to a Supreme Court decision that weakened the Voting Rights Act.

entry.title: Some school districts switch to electric buses as diesel prices soar
entry.summary: School districts that drive long distances are navigating record high diesel prices in different ways. Some have transitioned to electric or propane buses to ease the pinch.

entry.title: Tennessee governor pauses executions after Christa Pike survives 2 lethal injections
entry.summary: Reaction was swift after the execution of a Tennessee woman was halted because she survived two lethal injections.
